say: At 8 PM, your app starts showing errors. The database is running fine. It just can't take any more connections.
show: At [8 PM,] your app starts showing *errors.* The database is running *fine.* It just can't take any more [connections.]

say: A connection is the open line between your app and its database, where your data lives. Every question travels over one. And opening a new one is slow, because the app has to say hello and log in first.
show: A *connection* is the open line between your app and its database, where your data lives. Every question travels over one. And opening a new one is [slow,] because the app has to say hello and log in first.

say: If every visitor's request opens its own connection, a busy evening means hundreds at once. But a database only allows so many. Postgres allows a hundred by default.
show: If every visitor's request opens its *own connection,* a busy evening means [hundreds at once.] But a database only allows so many. *Postgres* allows [a hundred] by default.

say: Go over the limit, and new connections get refused. Your users see errors.
show: Go over the limit, and new connections get [refused.] Your users see *errors.*

say: The fix is a connection pool. Your app opens a few connections, and keeps them open to reuse.
show: The fix is a [connection pool.] Your app opens a *few* connections, and keeps them open to *reuse.*

say: Each request borrows one, asks its question, and hands it back. If they're all busy, it waits its turn in line.
show: Each request [borrows one,] asks its question, and *hands it back.* If they're all busy, it waits its turn in line.

say: Like a taxi rank. The cabs are already waiting, so you just hop in, instead of waiting for a new one to drive over every time.

say: Most database libraries come with a pool. Use it, and keep the total across all your servers under the database's limit, with room to spare.
